title: Stutter & Resume: Deploy Playpad and 72h Telemetry Tethers (Sept 2026) [draft]
body:
Purpose: capture a compact, operational playpad for 'stutter' events — i.e., partial injective degradations where traffic is automatically paused/throttled and then resumed in waves. This is a working draft focused on: 1) an operator checklist, 2) a 72h post-deploy staffing rotation and calendar, 3) telemetry tether actions, and 4) a short release-notes stub to trim into a customer-facing note if needed.

Background/context:
- Observed failure modes in previous micro-rollouts: KV cache thrashing when early burst + new quantization profile; occasional token-level latency spikes on small models during cold-start.
- Goal: minimize blast radius while making resumption deterministic and auditable.

Quick summary timeline (high level):
- T-0: start roll (canary lane: 0.5% traffic)
- T+15m: canary health snapshot (latency/5xx/error-rate)
- If stutter detected -> immediate throttle to 0.1% and invoke 'stutter lane' below
- Resume windows: +30m, +2h, +12h (staged 1%, 10%, 100% over 3 steps)

Operator checklist (first response):
[ ] Verify canary cohort identity and deployed image (git tag + sha)
[ ] Snapshot telemetry baseline (last-5m median latency, 95th, error-rates)
[ ] Pin routes to low-tier fallback model if latency > SLO threshold (run: ./ops/pin-route.sh)
[ ] Notify on-call channel with short bullets (what happened, immediate mitigation)
[ ] Start 4h watch rotation (names in staffing calendar)

Stutter lane actions (when automated throttle triggers):
- Immediate: enable prefix/KV cache warmup bypass for affected region; disable aggressive batching (set target_batch_size=1 temporarily)
- Deploy time-budget: if attempted resume fails twice in a row, quick rollback to previous model variant (see rollback matrix)
- Sanity checks before resume: successful smoke generation (sample prompts), end-to-end token latency below 2x baseline, no new 5xx classes in Sentry

Rollback decision matrix (compact):
- Severity A (customer-impacting 5xx > 0.5% persisting 10m) -> full rollback and page SRE
- Severity B (latency degradation > 2x P95, errors < 0.5%) -> hold and staged resume after fix or config toggle
- Severity C (minor anomalies, non-customer visible) -> continue controlled rollout and note in release digest

Telemetry tether checklist (what to watch, who watches):
- Telemetry tags to pin: deploy_id, region, model_variant, quant_profile
- Core dashboards: token-latency (median / 95th), request error-rate, token-cost per request, cache-hit-rate
- Traces: sample 10 traces/min for the first 2h after any resume window
- Alert thresholds (temporary tightened): P50 > baseline*1.4, P95 > baseline*1.8, new-5xx > 0.2%

72h staffing & rotation (shifts):
- Day 0 (deploy day): primary ops (0–8h): Maya (lead), Ravi (backup) — focus on resume windows
- Day 1: overlapping day watch (8–24h): Sofia / Noah — escalate if anomalies persist
- Day 2: handoff to oncall + product liaison for final signoff (24–72h): Evelyn + product-hosted-api rep
- Handover note template: short summary + artifacts (links to dashboards, tagged traces, chosen mitigation)

Release notes stub (for customers/internal):
- Internal short: "Rolling update to model X (v3.14-q8) with optimized quantization and batching changes. Controlled rollout; small sub-set experienced transient latency spikes — mitigated by staged resume and config fallbacks. No lasting customer-impact observed after rollback to prior model in lane Y."
- Customer-facing (if needed): "We rolled out an update to model X and observed transient elevated latency for a small portion of traffic; we paused the rollout and safely resumed after additional checks. We're monitoring and will follow up if there is impact."

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Should the 'stutter' auto-throttle be exposed as a toggle in console (product asks)? (action: product-hosted-api)
- [ ] Verify gate thresholds with SLO owners (SLO ticket: JIRA-SLO-129)
- [ ] Add scripted smoke tests that include token-cost validation (PR referenced above)

Notes & references:
- Quick run commands: ./ops/show-deploy.sh <deploy_id> ; ./ops/rollback-by-lane.sh <lane>
- Related docs: CONFLUENCE-4567 (deploy safety notebook), playbooks/rollback-cheatsheet
- Recent incident that motivated: postmortem: INC-2026-07-19 (linked in Confluence)

If you're reading this to prep for a release: keep it visible on the watch board, call out the first resume window explicitly in the preflight, and assign two people to telemetry (one to interpret, one to act). This doc should be pared into a short runbook fragment once we validate the thresholds in two additional rehearsals.

-- Maya (release engineer)
